- .claude/hooks/unattended_question_guard.py:_publish_attempts function (the live file, missing the `call_fits` inner function that the twin has at line ~797) | severity=critical | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The live file's `_publish_attempts` checks the 24s budget only at the top of each attempt loop, reserving time for a single 6s call. Each attempt can make up to three sequential 6s calls (comments GET + comment POST + label POST) without intermediate budget checks, totaling up to 18s per attempt. With 1s and 2s backoffs between attempts, total wall time can reach ~37s, well past the 30s hook wiring timeout. The previous review round identified this exact defect as a consensus BLOCKER finding (deepseek / openai / qwen / z-ai), and the round-1 fix in commit `ed774a4` added the `call_fits` per-call check to the twin at `workflow-templates/.claude/hooks/unattended_question_guard.py:797` but did NOT apply the same fix to the live file.
  WHY: When a session hits the cap during slow GitHub API responses (e.g., a GET takes 5s, a POST times out at 6s), the live file's `_publish_attempts` will keep making calls past the 30s process timeout. The hook process is killed before it can record `cap_blocker: pending` (see the second finding below), so the next `Stop` in the session cannot retry. The chain silently stalls, defeating the entire purpose of the cap blocker.
- .claude/hooks/unattended_question_guard.py:publish_cap_blocker function (the live file, around line 743-746; the twin stores pending before the call at line ~756) | severity=critical | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The live file's `publish_cap_blocker` stores `cap_blocker: pending` state AFTER `_publish_attempts` returns, not before. The twin version stores pending BEFORE the first call, so a hook killed mid-publish (by the 30s wiring timeout, a process signal, or any other termination) leaves a retry for the next `Stop`. The test `test_pending_is_stored_before_the_first_call` at `tests/test_unattended_question_guard.py:1018-1037` directly verifies this behavior by injecting a runner that raises `KeyboardInterrupt` on the first call and asserts `seen == [guard.CAP_BLOCKER_PENDING]`. This test would FAIL against the live file because the live file does not store pending before the first call.
  WHY: A hook killed mid-publish leaves no pending marker in the state file. The next `Stop` in the session finds no pending state and does not retry. The chain silently stalls — the exact failure mode the cap blocker is meant to prevent.
